subject: Avalon: request for inference integration diagrams, isolation and threat summary
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@avalonhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@avalonhealth.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: diagrams + isolation & threat summary for inference integration

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As part of our procurement packet we need a short technical bundle describing how Redwood will integrate with Avalon’s VPC and what isolation guarantees you can provide for our PHI-bearing workloads. Specifically Avalon’s security review asked for:

- A network diagram showing tenant egress patterns, control plane/data plane demarcation, and any peering or transit points.
- A short appendix describing the isolation model (sidecars, tenant slices, KV cache scoping, operator access controls).
- A 1–2 page threat-model summary focused on lateral movement, egress exfiltration, and supply-chain/third-party libraries used in the runtime.

Can you send a consolidated packet by Monday? Also include any evidence artifacts (Ingress/egress ACL examples, HSM/KMS integration notes). Prefer PDF(s) plus any diagram PNGs.

Tom Reyes
Director, Platform Security
Avalon Health

Attachment: (none)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jul 2028 19:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: RFP: diagrams + isolation & threat summary for inference integration

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. We can produce the packet and will send a consolidated bundle by Monday EOD.

Action plan:
- Ben: produce the annotated network diagram (VPC peering, sidecar placement, egress lanes, bastion access patterns).
- Kimberly: write the isolation appendix and the 1–2 page threat-model summary targeting the three vectors you called out.
- Irene: include notes on KMS/HSM integration and operator access controls (audit logs, session recording).

Two quick clarifying points for Avalon:
1) Is your preference that Redwood’s sidecar runs in your customer VPC (customer-sidecar) vs Redwood-managed tenant enclaves? We’ll prepare both sketches but a preferred topology helps reduce churn.
2) Any specific compliance artifacts Raven (your procurement system) requires (SOC-2 report ID, encryption attestations)?

I’ll coordinate a short 30-min review once we have a draft.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security Programs, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Subject: Draft: annotated network diagram + follow-ups

Neha / team — attaching the first sketches. Highlights included in the diagram:

- Control plane (Redwood-managed) is in our control plane VPC with strict peering to the customer VPC; all model artifacts are pinned to model-versioned storage with signed URIs.
- Data plane inference nodes (GPU pools) can be deployed as: 
  * customer-sidecar deployment (sidecar VMs in Avalon subnets, requests route to Redwood runtime over mTLS), or
  * Redwood-hosted tenant enclave (separate subnets in our managed VPC with dedicated egress lanes).
- KV cache scoping: per-tenant logical KV namespaces; caches live on the inference node and are flushed on model version changes or explicit tenant eviction.
- Egress lanes: customer-determined egress (preferred) via VPC peering and route tables; fallback is Redwood egress with restricted NAT and egress filtering.
- Operator access: strictly zero-bastion by default; operator actions require just-in-time (JIT) access with recorded sessions and approval workflow.

Questions for Avalon (quick):
1) Do you require customer-managed NATs for egress or would a Redwood-curated egress allowlist be acceptable for certified destinations?
2) For sidecar deployments, will you allow AWS IAM role chaining for startup (we use instance-role to bootstrap sidecar)?

Attachment: avalon-inference-vpc-and-egress-diagram.png (diagram, 1.2 MB)

Thanks — Ben

Date: Sat, 16 Jul 2028 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Isolation appendix + threat-model summary (draft)

Tom — attached is the requested isolation appendix and the threat-model summary. Executive highlights below:

Isolation model (short):
- Network: Strong demarcation between control plane and data plane. Customer traffic remains in customer subnets unless you elect Redwood-hosted enclaves. Sidecar option places runtime in your VPC using mTLS + service mesh policies to limit lateral calls.
- Compute: Per-tenant logical slices, no shared process-level memory across tenants. We use kernel-level namespaces and container-level seccomp/memory hardening on inference nodes.
- KV/Cache: Cache entries are keyed by tenant id + model-version; all caches are ephemeral and encrypted at rest. Cache eviction and TTLs can be configured per-customer for high-sensitivity workloads.
- Operator boundaries: RBAC with per-action audit logs; emergency access is JIT, multi-approver, and recorded.

Threat-model summary (1 page):
- Lateral movement: mitigations include strict host-level segmentation, mTLS-only service mesh, per-tenant network policies, and container sandboxing. We simulate adversary paths quarterly and expose red-team results to customers under NDA.
- Egress exfiltration: egress is permit-list only by default; for customer-sidecar we recommend customer-managed egress. For Redwood-hosted egress we enforce destination allowlists, packet inspection metadata logging, and flow-level alerts.
- Supply chain: the runtime uses pinned third-party libraries (SBOM available). We run SLSA-style build attestations and kernel/hardware attestation on startup; we also support FIPS-validated crypto modules where required.

Attachment: isolation-model-appendix.pdf (PDF, 640 KB)
Attachment: threat-model-summary-avalon.docx (DOCX, 95 KB)

Irene — adding a short KMS/HSM note inline: we support customer-managed KMS through AWS KMS or external HSM (PKCS#11) for keys that sign model artifacts and control plane credentials. Audit logs for key operations can be exported to your SIEM.

Kimberly Park
Senior Security Architect, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
